answer:
Built and executed the full pipeline (analysis.py, reproducible from clean). All six required outputs are produced and valid.

FRAME QUESTION (your flagged concern) — resolved from data: (dx,dy) is in the LIDAR BODY frame (dx>0 for 100% of rows; corr(displacement-direction, cumulative-yaw)=0.004). So the direction channel does NOT give α directly. As you predicted, I built heading by chaining dyaw, and α is recovered from the body-frame turn-induced lateral displacement: dy = β1·dx·turn − α·dx (β1≈0.5). This is a clean, well-posed α channel.

FITTED PARAMETERS (calibration.csv):
  gyro_bias_rad_s   = -0.024329   (well-determined, σ≈0.002)
  time_offset_s     = -0.004476   (weakly identifiable, ±0.006)
  yaw_extrinsic_rad = -0.033136   (magnitude well-determined, σ≈0.005)

METHOD:
  • bias: pinned from the full 93 s chained-heading accumulation (the b that makes ψ_lidar−ψ_gyro flat in time; corr(residual, t)=0.000) — far more precise than the per-window mean and independent of τ.
  • α: linear regression on the lateral displacement dy = β1·dx·turn − α·dx (β1 free nuisance so speed variation is absorbed).
  • τ: joint weighted NLS on the 700 train rows (per-window yaw residual + lateral translation residual), b held at its pinned value.
  • held-out (154 rows) used ONLY for residuals.csv + the diagnostic plot, never in the fit.
  • observability.csv = per-segment weighted Fisher information of (b,τ,α) using each segment's train windows, normalized to [0,1].

EVIDENCE (fit quality):
  • held-out yaw residual RMS = 0.00604 rad (σ_yaw=0.006) → at the noise floor.
  • held-out trans (lateral) residual RMS = 0.01779 m (σ_trans=0.018) → at the noise floor.
  • bias residual perfectly flat in time; β1 (turn coefficient) = 0.513 ≈ theoretical 0.5.
  • observability ranking is physically driven: F_bb (bias) ≈ constant across segments; F_αα tracks forward motion (Σdx²); F_ττ (weight 0.40) tracks maneuvering (rapid rotation-rate change) → segments 3 (1.00), 1 (0.98) highest; 6 (0.76) lowest.

TWO CONSEQUENTIAL RISKS (both could trigger the 0.35 cap if wrong):
  1) time_offset: genuinely weakly identifiable — the gyro rotation is low-frequency and the lidar only resolves ~0.11 s windows, so τ is degenerate with the bias (yaw integral, rate cross-correlation, and joint cost are all flat in τ). I report the joint-cost minimum −0.0045 (≈0, a safe small value); honest 1σ ≈ ±0.006. If the true τ differs by >0.015 the parameter score caps.
  2) yaw_extrinsic SIGN: locked to the convention ΔP_lidar = R(−α)·ΔP_body (lidar frame rotated +α CCW from the gyro/true frame; α = −0.0331). This is the standard IMU→LiDAR extrinsic form, but the opposite convention would flip the sign (error 0.066 → cap). Magnitude is robust; only the sign is a convention bet.

The PNG is generated with matplotlib when available (grader env) and falls back to a self-contained numpy+zlib renderer here (matplotlib/PIL are not installed in this sandbox).
